ai.description: Günther's burrowing snake reaches 30–40 cm. It is uniform dark brown or purplish-black with a glossy sheen. The tail ends in a distinct, flattened, heavily keeled terminal shield.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Plectrurus guentheri* is best distinguished by its unique tail tip, which features a large, flattened, shield-like scale that is distinctly notched or bidentate.
ai.habitat: Günther's Burrowing Snake inhabits the moist evergreen forests and shola grasslands of the Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 1,000 and 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: Günther's burrowing snake is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending most of its life underground where it feeds on earthworms and soft-bodied invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Plectrurus guentheri* is ovoviviparous, giving birth to small litters of 2–4 live young. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: Plectrurus guentheri is endemic to the southern Western Ghats, primarily occurring in the high-elevation shola forests of Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
